newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends soft on dollar short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends soft on dollar short-covering.

text.p: The Mexican peso retained earlier softness at the close on Friday following what traders said was speculation and dollar short-covering ahead of U.S. key economic data due next week.
"The peso slid this morning on speculation, the sliding Dow Jones and higher U.S. long bond yields," a trader said. "Then when it reached a certain level, it stayed there."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended two and 2.8 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.8910/7.8960 and 7.8900/7.8930 per dollar.
The Dow Jones ended down 53.38 points at 6,738.87, while the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was off 5/32 to yield 7.14 percent.

Traders also put speculation and demand for dollars down to brokers hedging against strong results for key U.S. economic data next week, which could lead to pressure on the U.S. bond market and a weaker peso.
Dealers said they would closely watch U.S. first quarter GDP and employment and unemployment data.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier ended 3.6 centavos weaker at 7.8790/7.8830 per dollar.
